collection.description: A child asks a villager who thanks the water whenever they fill a jar whether the water can hear.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Every time (subject) fills (subject.his/her) jar at the water, (subject.he/she) says "thank you" to it. Quietly, the way you'd thank someone passing you a bowl. Today (friend) is with (subject.him/her) and wants to know: "Can the water hear you?"

a.name: Answer A
a.text: "I don't know," says (subject), honestly. "Some people think so. Some people don't. I just like saying it." (friend) thinks about this, then leans over the water and says "thank you" too, very loudly, just in case it's a little hard of hearing.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: "What do you think?" asks (subject). (friend) looks at the water for a long time. "I think it hears the fish," (friend.he/she) says. "So it can probably hear us." (subject) agrees that this sounds reasonable. On the way home, (friend) thanks a puddle, two coconuts and (builder), a very surprised builder.
